content_preview.title: DeepSpeed 0.19.8 Removes Elastic Training, Progressive Layer Dropping and Apex AMP, Turning Leftover Configs Into Errors
content_preview.summary: DeepSpeed 0.19.8 removes elastic training, Progressive Layer Dropping, Apex AMP and graph harvesting; configs that still set them now raise DeepSpeedConfigError.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The [v0.19.8 release of DeepSpeed](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/releases/tag/v0.19.8), the distributed training library, was published on October 20, 2026. Its changelog includes a run of removals: entries titled "Remove elastic training", "Remove Progressive Layer Dropping (PLD) support", "Deprecate APEX amp", "Deprecate sparse_gradients", "Deprecate legacy curriculum learning" and "Deprecate and remove graph harvesting". editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News piece (680 words, within the 400-1200 range) with logical structure: release, tracking-issue context, per-removal detail, fail-loudly design, other additions, limitations. Precise and appropriately technical.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 8 sources are github.com (on allowlist, line 1131) and all are first-party DeepSpeed project pages; no independent outlet exists for this story and none is cited (documented; News format carries no independence requirement). Snapshots source-0..7.html.gz (all HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns) were read as a sanity check, then every source was re-fetched live as raw text via the GitHub API (releases, issues, pulls). source-0 (release v0.19.8): published_at 2026-10-20T15:21:47Z (matches article date; snapshot datetime identical). Changelog lists, with verbatim titles, 'Remove elastic training' (#8563), 'Remove Progressive Layer Dropping (PLD) support' (#8562), 'Deprecate APEX amp' (#8564), 'Deprecate sparse_gradients' (#8504), 'Deprecate legacy curriculum learning' (#8566), 'Deprecate and remove graph harvesting' (#8579), plus 'Add DualPipeV', 'Add KLXPU (KUNLUNXIN XPU) accelerator', '[muon] Per-head Newton-Schulz for attention projections', 'Add an opt-in fused Triton RMSNorm for Llama-style Hugging Face models', 'Speed up import deepspeed by deferring heavy imports and import-time work'. The release body is a bare list of PR titles with no migration guide (confirms the What We Don't Know claim). Shipped-in-release check: all six PRs are merged into master (merged_at: #8504 2026-09-17T04:04Z, #8566 2026-09-17, #8564 2026-09-17, #8562 2026-09-18, #8563 2026-09-18, #8579 2026-09-25), all before the v0.19.8 release (created 2026-10-19) and after v0.19.7 (2026-09-16T22:00Z), and all six appear in the release notes; nothing is presented as shipped that was not. source-1 (issue #8489, 'Deprecate unused DeepSpeed features'): the sentence 'Tracking issue for retiring unused / unmaintained DeepSpeed features so the runtime, docs, tests, and packaging stay consistent.' is verbatim; #8490 'Merged 2026-09-12' removing compression library, 1-bit Adam/Lamb, 0/1 Adam, MiCS, Nebula with '+169 / -8,298' confirmed. The issue checklist and comments (last activity 2026-09-30) still show PLD, Apex AMP, elastic training, graph_harvesting and legacy curriculum as 'No PR'/unchecked and sparse_gradients as Open, confirming the article's caveat that the checklist predates the merges. source-2 (#8563): elasticity block, batch-size solver, DSElasticAgent, --elastic_training removed; 'Reject a leftover elasticity block with DeepSpeedConfigError instead of silently training without it' (article quote 'instead of silently training without it' verbatim); 'zero' issues outside the org for the config pair; model-parallel/pipeline-parallel assertions; zero_optimization.elastic_checkpoint explicitly not touched; PR-body diffstat '21 files changed, 48 insertions(+), 1475 deletions(-)' matches the article (live API now reports 47/1474, a one-line drift; the article attributes the figure to the PR's own report, which is accurate). source-3 (#8564): 'Existing amp configurations - including disabled, empty, or null blocks - now raise DeepSpeedConfigError, directing users to fp16, bf16, or torch_autocast'; native PyTorch AMP and optional apex.optimizers.FusedAdam remain supported; confirmed. source-4 (#8504): sparse_gradients flag removed and raises DeepSpeedConfigError; 'essentially deprecated as we don't see use cases for it as much anymore' verbatim; sum-based row selection with the [1.0, -1.0] example silently dropping updates; Embedding(sparse=True) unchanged at ZeRO stage 0; confirmed. The article omits the PR #8504 merge date; I verified the discrepancy: the tracking issue says 'Merged 2026-09-16' while the API gives 2026-09-17T04:04:30Z, the same instant in different time zones, so omission is correct and no date in the article is wrong. source-5 (#8562): PLD scheduler/config/engine/tests/tutorial removed; 'Reject any configuration containing progressive_layer_drop with DeepSpeedConfigError, including disabled, empty, null, and "auto" values, instead of silently training without PLD'; confirmed. source-6 (#8566): legacy top-level curriculum_learning removed, superseded by the retained Data Efficiency library, error message points to the replacement; article quote 'now fails at parse time instead of silently training without the feature' verbatim; confirmed. source-7 (#8579): graph_harvesting with any value including false/null raises DeepSpeedConfigError; confirmed. Error class: all six removals raise DeepSpeedConfigError and none merely warns, so the title's 'Turning Leftover Configs Into Errors' and the 'fails at startup' framing hold. All six PRs reference #8489, supporting the 'tracked clean-up' framing. The article names no contributors. Body URLs and article.sources match exactly (no orphans). No suspicious_patterns in the manifest and no injection-style text seen.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, name, quote and attribution traced to a cited source; no errors found. The release page uses 'Deprecate' in four titles while the PR bodies describe removal and config rejection; the article quotes the titles accurately and states the removal behavior per the PR descriptions.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive; no editorializing or AI self-reference. Impact claims are hedged ('configuration files may need editing') and the article states that no source quantifies affected users beyond the maintainers' own usage scan.
editor_notes.originality: No prior DeepSpeed coverage in the archive (only an unrelated TRL article mentions it). Distinct topic.
concerns: All sources are first-party project pages; no independent outlet. Acceptable for a News item about a project's own release and documented here.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced release coverage with verbatim quotes and correct attribution of each removal to its PR and to the shipped release. Approved without corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate breaking-change coverage for DeepSpeed users, a defined developer audience
